== Biography ==

Dorothy, also known as Princess Dorothy, travels through the Land of Oz alongside a group of companions that includes the Wizard, Uncle Henry, the Shaggy Man, and Omby Amby. She and her fellow travelers ride away from the Cuttenclip village along an indistinct path until reaching a sign-post marking the main road, where the group continues pleasantly through pretty farming country. At a fork in the road, a sign-post reading "THIS WAY TO FUDDLECUMJIG" prompts Dorothy to observe that this is where they turn. During these travels she rides a horse made entirely of wood, one that never gets tired nor cares to lie down; Dorothy herself is not quite sure whether it ever sleeps, though it is certain the horse never does so when anyone is around.

Along the road, Dorothy inquires what the Flutterbudgets are like, though she is told it is no trouble to find places if one keeps to the right road. When a poor man they encounter cries out in distress after pricking his finger with a needle and seeing blood, Dorothy follows the Wizard, Uncle Henry, the Shaggy Man, and Omby Amby to his assistance as quickly as she can, and asks what has happened.

According to her own account, given after she, Toto, and Billina return to the signpost camp where the rest of the party has waited anxiously through the day tracking her footprints, Dorothy reports having eaten a wheelbarrow and a piano and having lunched with a King, a claim that leaves Aunt Em doubtful. In recounting her day to Aunt Em and Uncle Henry, she describes visits to Utensia, Bunbury, and Bunnybury, though this account reflects Dorothy's own perspective rather than confirmed fact.

The travelers' route later takes them through Flutterbudget Center, where the residents are said to work themselves into panic over dangers that never come to pass, before reaching the Winkie Country, where Dorothy's party lunches with the Tin Woodman at his tin castle and tours his tin gardens and fish pond.

== Narrative role ==

Dorothy, traveling with Toto and Billina, returns to the signpost camp, where the Wizard's party has spent the day anxiously waiting after tracking her footprints there. Back among the group, she announces that she is not hungry, having already eaten a wheelbarrow and a piano and lunched with a King — a claim that leaves Aunt Em disbelieving.

She goes on to recount her day's adventures to Aunt Em and Uncle Henry, describing her visits to Utensia, Bunbury, and Bunnybury. As the journey continues, she and the Wizard discuss airships, and the Wizard reveals that he is working on a magic recipe meant to keep airships from ever reaching the Land of Oz.

Later, Dorothy's party passes through Flutterbudget Center, where the residents work themselves into panic over hypothetical dangers that never occur.

Afterward, Glinda the Good casts a spell rendering all of Oz invisible to outsiders, and Dorothy sends a farewell note confirming that Oz is now cut off from the rest of the world forever.

== Personality ==

Dorothy shows marked curiosity about unfamiliar places and people, asking directly what the Flutterbudgets are like when she has never encountered them before. She is also observant, noticing and reading the sign-post that redirects the party toward Fuddlecumjig before anyone else remarks on it.

When Uncle Henry falls and the others rush to help him, Dorothy follows as quickly as she can, indicating a readiness to respond when someone in her company is in distress. She also presses further when the injured man's account seems incomplete, asking what has truly happened rather than accepting the first explanation — a small but consistent trait of wanting to understand a situation fully before moving on.

== Relationships ==

'''[[Ozma]]''' — friend. The pair travel together through the farming country beyond Cuttenclip, and it was Ozma who laid out the trip and "'vised" Dorothy's party to see the Rigmaroles next, which could indicate a trusted bond between them.

'''[[Aunt Em]]''' — family. Dorothy addresses her directly as "Aunt Em" during their journey together, as when she laughingly tells her, "I can't say 'zactly, Aunt Em, what they are," a familiarity that suggests a family tie.

'''[[Billina]]''' — friend. Billina travels at Dorothy's side, marching with her and Toto in the center of the spoon brigade at Utensia, which seems to point to a close companionship.

'''[[Wizard]]''' — friend. The Wizard journeys with Dorothy's party and rushes to help alongside her when trouble arises on the road, with Dorothy following "as quickly as she could," suggesting the two are allies within the traveling group.

'''[[Toto]]''' — friend. Toto stays close to Dorothy throughout the journey, accompanying her and Billina at the center of the spoon brigade's hollow square, which could indicate a steady, loyal companionship between them.
